channel.title: The Kyiv Independent - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Kyiv Independent (kyivindependent.com)

item.title: Drone crashes at Polish military base, operator detained
item.description: The drone, a small commercially available model, crashed at the 1st Air Cavalry Battalion's base in the Lodz province after snagging a tree. No damage was recorded, the Polish military police reported.

item.title: The Ukrainian origins of avant-garde artist Kazimir Malevich, long mislabelled as Russian
item.description: In 2016, Natalia Zabolotna, then director of the Kyiv-based art gallery Mystetskyi Arsenal, proposed naming Kyiv’s main airport, Boryspil International Airport, after the famous avant-garde artist Kazimir Malevich.Her idea was far from eccentric. Across Europe, airports serve as sites of cultural self-definition, carrying the names of compatriots

item.title: Moldovan president rejects Nobel Peace Prize nomination, says Ukrainian POWs deserve it instead
item.description: "Today, I was watching Ukrainian (prisoners of war) who returned home from Russia, and these are the people who deserve the Peace Prize," Moldovan President Maia Sandu said.

item.title: Ukraine calendar: What will happen this week
item.description: Editor's note: This article is a shortened on-site version of KI Insights' public newsletter, The Week Ahead, covering events from February 9-15. Sign up here to start your week with an agenda of Ukraine-related events delivered directly to your inbox every week. Audio version of The Week

item.title: Zelensky announces Air Force personnel changes amid regional air defense concerns
item.description: The changes will target units that are responsible for intercepting Russian unmanned aerial vehicles, according to President Volodymyr Zelensky.

item.title: Ukraine war latest: Kyiv carried out 3 offensive operations in 2025, including 2 inside Russia, Syrskyi says
item.description: Live coverage of Russia’s war against Ukraine with breaking news and frontline updates, updated 10 times today. Ukraine launched three offensive operations in 2025, Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi said on Feb. 6, according to RBC Ukraine.

item.title: US approves $185 million sale of spare parts for Ukraine’s vehicles and weapon systems
item.description: The U.S. Department of State on Feb. 6 approved a potential $185 million “Foreign Military Sale” to Ukraine for spare parts and related equipment to support U.S.-supplied vehicles and weapon systems.

item.title: Drone discovered on Moldovan territory near Ukraine border
item.description: An unidentified drone was found on Moldovan territory on Feb. 6, Moldovan authorities reported.

item.title: Zelensky's ex-chief of staff Yermak meets top officials, keeps his influence, investigation shows
item.description: Some of the meetings could have been linked to Yermak's role in a corruption case involving state nuclear power monopoly Energoatom, the biggest corruption investigation during Zelensky's presidency, Ukrainska Pravda reported.

item.title: Russia launches mass attack on Ukraine, triggers emergency power outages
item.description: Russia carried out a mass attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure in the early hours of Feb. 7, triggering emergency power outages across most regions, Ukraine's state grid operator Ukrenergo said.
